disclaimer: Monitoring and reporting aid. Not legal advice. Not an official OCC form.

findings.description: Reserve asset value must at all times equal or exceed the outstanding issuance value.
findings.citation: 12 CFR 15.11(a)(1)(iii); reserve asset value as defined in Table 1 to 15.11(e), rows 15 to 17.
findings.rule_notes: Reserve asset value = total reserve assets minus outstanding repurchase-agreement liabilities. Rows flagged is_repo_liability are treated as liabilities, so supply them or coverage is overstated when the issuer has repos outstanding. Only a snapshot is checked, but the rule applies at all times. A shortfall also triggers 15.11(g): notify the OCC on any day reserves fall below the minimum, no new issuance until restored, and liquidation after 15 consecutive business days (the tool cannot see history; see RW-NOT-001).

findings.description: At least a minimum share of reserve assets must be held as demand deposits (or other deposits withdrawable on request at any time), share accounts payable on demand, or money in an account with a Federal Reserve Bank.
findings.rule_notes: The input flag is_immediately_available must be set only for assets in the categories above; the tool trusts it. The denominator is total reserve assets (repo liabilities excluded).

findings.description: Exposure to any one counterparty may not exceed a maximum share of reserve assets, except for exposures to the United States Government, to an appropriate custodian from assets held in its custody, and from centrally cleared repurchase and reverse repurchase agreements.
findings.rule_notes: Exempt exposures are marked with the reserves column concentration_exemption (us_government, custodian, centrally_cleared_repo); they stay in the denominator but not in any counterparty's numerator. The tool cannot verify the conditions of 15.11(d) (the issuer identifies itself to the custodian, the custodian commits to GENIUS Act section 10, and ongoing due diligence), so an exemption is taken as asserted by the issuer. Exposure is measured as the sum of reserve rows per counterparty over total reserve assets.

findings.description: A timely redemption may not exceed a maximum number of business days following the redemption request.
findings.citation: 12 CFR 15.12(a)(2) and 15.12(c)(1) (two business days); business day per 12 CFR 15.2.
findings.rule_notes: The two-business-day limit and the definition of when redemption occurs (15.12(a)(2)) are from the codified text supplied. The clock-start rule (valid order plus satisfied conditions such as onboarding, 15.12(a)(1)) and the business-day definition (15.2) were described in the final rule preamble and are not in the text supplied. The counting convention, near-breach margin and handling of open, rejected and cancelled requests are owner decisions, not text from the rule. Discretionary limits on redemption can only be imposed by the regulator (15.12(c)(2)); the tool does not model them.

findings.description: Redemption requests in excess of a share of outstanding issuance value in a single 24-hour period require notice to the OCC within 24 hours.
findings.rule_notes: A duty to notify, not a violation: the finding always passes and is a WARNING when notice is due; the tool cannot see whether notice was given. Every request received counts, whatever its later status. The 24-hour period is applied as a rolling window starting at each request; the rule text does not say whether it means rolling or calendar-day windows. Outstanding issuance is the latest supply snapshot, for a single brand of stablecoin.
